steps.content: Starting with Random Forest to establish a baseline performance with a reasonable number of trees and limiting depth will help assess generalization accuracy.

The Random Forest model with 100 estimators and a maximum depth of 10 achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95731 with a standard deviation of 0.01709. The validation accuracy is 0.94152, which is reasonably high.
Increasing the number of estimators and exploring a deeper tree will likely improve performance by allowing the model to learn more complex patterns.

The Random Forest model with 200 estimators and a maximum depth of 15 achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.96231, which is an improvement over the previous configuration. The validation accuracy increased to 0.94737. The standard deviation is also stable, suggesting reliability in this configuration.
Testing a larger maximum depth with a slightly reduced number of estimators may help capture more intricate patterns while avoiding overfitting.

The Random Forest model with 150 estimators and a maximum depth of 20 did not improve upon the previous best configuration, maintaining the same mean cross-validated accuracy and validation accuracy. Given that no improvements were observed, it suggests this configuration is not beneficial.

steps.final_recommendation: Use the Random Forest model with 200 estimators and a maximum depth of 15, as it provided the highest accuracy and stability among the configurations tested.
